label: Dry Lab
rows: Inefficient sequence screening and unstable low-copy signals
Prof. Tianyi Zhao’s advice → Introduced DNABERT-6 for systematic candidate-sequence screening.
Prof. Xingfang Li’s advice → Added molecular dynamics simulations to prioritize promising candidates for wet-lab validation.

label: Wet Lab
rows: Prof. X. Chris Le’s advice → Shifted to a portable one-pot RPA–CRISPR/Cas12a method.
One-pot reactions showed reduced activity and component interference
Prof. Tsan-Yuk Lam’s advice → Optimized Mg²⁺, pH, and primer–crRNA ratios with single-factor experiments and controls.

label: Software
rows: Weak fluorescence and background interference complicated signal reading
Prof. Yingtao Zhang’s advice → Used YOLOv8n + OpenCV for fluorescence recognition and background-noise reduction.
Multiple detection results were difficult to manage and display
Multichannel engineering and user needs → Updated the app for multi-tube recognition, fluorescence curves, and mobile results.

label: Hardware
rows: Laboratory reactions were difficult to reproduce in field settings
Prof. Zheng Hu’s advice → Integrated stable temperature control and fluorescence acquisition into a portable device.
Single-channel testing could not meet frontline multiplex needs
Nursing home and kindergarten feedback → Upgraded to a second-generation multichannel instrument.
More channels increased size and thermal-interference challenges
Prof. Ying Mou’s advice → Designed a rotating 15-position chamber with an independent, thermally isolated lysis region.
